Applied AI - San Francisco

**About the Team**

We are building AI systems that help people tackle complex, consequential work in the legal industry. Law demands careful reasoning, precise language, and sound judgment: understanding the facts, identifying the right questions, weighing competing interpretations, and helping clients decide what to do next. We see an opportunity for AI to help legal professionals work with greater rigor and focus more of their time on the problems that matter most.

Our team works across Research, Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market to build AI capabilities and products for legal work. Our customers include the top law firms in the world as well as in-house legal departments of some of the largest businesses in the world. We translate the realities of practice into evaluations, training signals, and useful tools, with the ambition of making AI a trusted part of how lawyers research, analyze, draft, and advise.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role at the intersection of legal practice and AI development. * Enjoy working directly with AI tools, exploring their limits, and testing ideas systematically. You can collaborate closely with technical teams and communicate clearly across disciplines.
* Take ownership in ambiguous settings and are willing to build the first version of an evaluation, reference document, rubric, or workflow, then improve it through feedback.
* Care deeply about the quality and consequences of legal work, and are motivated by the opportunity to help shape how AI supports the profession.

**Especially Strong Candidates May Also Have:**

* Experience designing evaluations, benchmarks, datasets, or review frameworks for legal work or frontier AI systems.
* A track record of improving legal workflows through technology, knowledge management, automation, or new ways of working.
* Experience training or supervising lawyers, developing practice guidance, or translating complex legal concepts for different audiences.

Position Summary
  
  
In this position, the Soil Health Research Associate works on a study to assess the effects of solar panels on soil health and microclimate at various sites across the continental USA. The Soil Health Research Associate performs soil sampling, field measurements, laboratory analyses, data processing, and report writing to support a multi-site investigation comparing soils below solar panels with adjacent control areas. This position operates within established policies and procedures, or by referring to the supervisor's guidelines, and contributes to quality control, laboratory safety, and task prioritization for the project.

jobs.title: Research Associate / Senior Research Associate, Evidence Base (Applications Development)
jobs.description:
Themis Bios is building the measurement layer for modern biology. Our single-cell RNA-seq technology is designed to make transcriptomic readouts routine, quantitative, and scalable — so scientists can ask harder questions and trust the answers.

We are looking for a Research Associate or Senior Research Associate to join Applications Development and own the cell biology at the front of our workflows. This is a hands-on, bench-first role: you will grow the cells, build the models, and turn living systems into single-cell samples that read cleanly on our platform. Your first focus is the Evidence Base: running the drug-perturbation experiments behind a growing atlas of how human primary cells and organoids respond to compounds. You will work alongside our Product Development team, and your culture work and sample prep will be the foundation the rest of the applications work is built on.

It is a good fit for someone who takes real pride in cell culture and technique, wants their bench work to feed a product, and brings hands-on drug screening experience they want to build on with single-cell readouts.

What you'll do

* **Cell culture.** Culture primary human PBMCs (thaw, rest and T-cell activation, e.g. anti-CD3/CD28) and gut organoids, with iPSC-derived models as needed — covering media preparation, plating, passaging, expansion, and cryopreservation, all under strict sterile technique.
* **Model quality.** Monitor culture health, morphology, and consistency; run routine checks and keep cultures to documented, reproducible standards so downstream results are trustworthy.
* **Sample preparation.** Prepare single-cell and single-nucleus samples from cells, organoids, and tissue — dissociation, viability and debris management, counting, and input QC — tuned for compatibility with the Themis scRNA-seq technology.
* **Experiment execution.** Execute cell-culture and sample-prep experiments, and run drug-perturbation studies (drug and molecule treatments across dose and time), under the direction of senior team members.
* **Drug plate preparation.** Prepare compound stocks in DMSO, serial dilutions, dose–response and combination layouts, and randomized plate maps with vehicle and control wells; keep compound inventory, storage and lot records current.
* Program and run liquid handlers (e.g. Agilent Bravo) for plate stamping, dilution and sample handling, and keep run logs.
* **Screening cadence.** Deliver about two drug plates a week on schedule, from cells to single-cell libraries, with QC at each step.
* **Data and records.** Generate high-quality, reproducible data and keep detailed, well-organized experimental records.
* **Protocols and QC.** Help turn working procedures into clear protocols and SOPs, and contribute to input-QC and sample-acceptance methods as workflows mature.
* **Lab operations.** Keep the lab running — inventory, reagent and consumable stocks, equipment upkeep and calibration — so experiments start on time and run clean.

  

What you'll bring

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, bioengineering, or a related field.
* 2–5 years of relevant industry or advanced academic laboratory experience (toward the upper end for the SRA level).
* Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture skills and disciplined sterile technique — together with drug screening, this is the core of the role.
* Hands-on drug or compound screening in mammalian cells — dose–response or plate-based assays, including preparing drug plates from stocks.
* Experience with primary immune cells (PBMCs preferred) and one or more of: 3D / organoid culture, or iPSC culture and differentiation.
* Sample-prep experience — dissociating cells, organoids, or tissue into high-quality single-cell suspensions, or a clear aptitude to learn it quickly.
* Careful technique with complex biological workflows, and a track record of generating reproducible data and troubleshooting experiments.
* Highly organized, with strong attention to detail and clear documentation habits.
* Comfortable in a dynamic startup environment with evolving priorities.

  

Strongly preferred

* Experience with single-cell genomics workflows (e.g. scRNA-seq, droplet or bead-based systems, barcoding / cell-hashing methods).
* Experience writing or adapting liquid-handler methods (e.g. Agilent Bravo, Hamilton, Echo) or other high-throughput sample handling.

  

Nice to have

* Experience with NGS library prep and QC methods (Bioanalyzer, TapeStation, Qubit, fragment analysis).
* Basic data-analysis skills (e.g. Python, R, or standard analysis tools) for exploring experimental results.
* Prior work in an assay-development, applications, or product-development lab.

  

What success looks like

* Cultures and models are healthy, consistent, and ready when the team needs them.
* Single-cell samples go into the workflow at high quality, with QC that holds up run to run.
* Data is reproducible and records are clear enough that others can build on the work.
* Throughput and reliability of the applications team go up because of how you run the bench.
* Drug plates go out on schedule, about two a week, with plate-map and dosing errors near zero and vehicle-control variability within spec.
* Each new model and plate workflow has an SOP someone else can run from.
* You operate with growing independence, flag issues early, and reinforce a culture of rigor and accountability.

The laboratory of Dr. Jeannie Chen at the Zilkha Neurogenetic Institute, Keck School of Medicine of USC, is seeking a highly motivated Research Associate to study phototransduction in rod and cone photoreceptors and the mechanisms underlying retinal degeneration and blindness. This NIH-funded laboratory uses rodent models and cell culture to investigate photoreceptor function, calcium signaling, inherited retinal diseases, GPCR biology, and protein misfolding and aggregation.

The successful candidate will develop and conduct independent research projects under the PI’s guidance, including designing and performing experiments and analyzing and interpreting data. Responsibilities also include presenting research findings, taking a leading role in writing manuscripts for publication, contributing to grant proposals, and supporting laboratory quality control, safety standards, and animal protocols.

The ideal candidate will be a creative and self-motivated researcher with experience in molecular and cellular biology techniques, including PCR or qRT-PCR, Western blotting and protein analysis, retinal tissue preparation under light- and dark-adapted conditions, *in vitro* and *in vivo* experiments (mouse), cell culture, immunohistochemistry (IHC) and immunocytochemistry (ICC), calcium imaging, fluorescence and confocal microscopy, and image analysis. Experience in photoreceptor biology, phototransduction, calcium signaling, retinal degeneration, protein trafficking, or protein misfolding is particularly valuable. The candidate should work well in a collaborative environment and may have opportunities to mentor junior laboratory members.
